items.title: Websites Should Be Printable
items.summary: css, web
items.content:
If you have questions or thoughts on the post I'd love to hear about it!

I'm currently looking for work in the northeastern US. I'll be graduating with a BS in both Computer Science and Cyber Operations at the end of the school year.

I have worked in web application development and Java, and I have experience in Rust, C++, Python, and various other languages.

If you're curious about what I've done in the past, I keep up a short list of projects here or contact me to give me a place to send my resume.

I figure anyone who reads my posts will have an interesting offer, so all leads are appreciated!

I read a lot of printed papers these days. While I enjoy reading on a laptop as much as the next guy, marking up a printed document engages me better. Also, there's something about sitting with a whiteboard and a printed document that makes me rightly feel like I'm doing something important. So I've been thinking about how to best allow others to enjoy this medium for content that I write.

Luckily for me, printed documents were a major focus of web design a while ago. You can print any webpage you like, by hitting CTRL-P and hoping your printer driver decides to cooperate today.

I tested this on my own webpage, foolishly thinking I would have a decent print job without any effort.

It wasn't great, although you can at least see all the content. The text was too big by about 2 levels, the header looks awful when printed, and my links look awfully gray in black-and-white. Totally unacceptable.

Luckily, the web community has had this aforementioned focus on printing documents from HTML pages. CSS has selectors to allow styling specifically printed content, and they can be useful. Here's my print-related snippet for this page now:

You can see the effects of this snippet by hitting CTRL-P or the print button on this page. Here's the functions this does for me, in order:

After attempting to optimize my website in this way, I am sympathetic for those who wouldn't prioritize printing. Hiding and showing all the right things in print took me a decent chunk of my morning. My site isn't very complex. I also doubt how many people regularly print webpages out. I might be the only one.

Still, if all your website consists of is text, allowing people to experience the text in their favorite medium is never a bad thing. The digital medium allows a lot of flexibility. The road to good software is paved with kindnesses from software engineers to their users. One day, perhaps someone shall find this kindness and smile, even if just for a fleeting moment. And that will be worth it.

Edit 2026-10-26: I was informed by a friend that this post ended up on the front page of HN and lobste.rs after I submitted it. Fun! Despite the several flaws I am now informed of in my CSS, I hope this article at least pushes a few to consider this medium more carefully. Thanks all for reading!

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-76654 📢 Source: kubernetes 💣 CVSS Score: 5.8 (MEDIUM) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True An NTLM coercion vulnerability exists on Windows nodes when the subPath supplied in a pod's volumeMounts is set to a symbolic link that points to an attacker-controlled network share. When a kubelet resolves symlinks, it does not reject a target that resolves to a UNC path. As a result, the kubelet will transparently attempt to authenticate to the share using NTLM. This allows an attacker to obtain the NetNTLMv2 hash of the account under which the kubelet is running. An attacker could then attempt to crack the hash to retrieve the corresponding password or relay it to impersonate the node, if the node is domain-joined. 📅 Published Date: 2026-10-26T22:29:23.944Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-76654
items.title_ko: CVE-2026-76654: Kubernetes Windows 노드 kubelet의 NTLM 강제 인증 취약점
items.summary_ko: Windows 노드에서 kubelet이 NTLM 인증을 시도하도록 강제되는 취약점입니다. 파드 volumeMounts의 subPath가 공격자가 제어하는 네트워크 공유(UNC 경로)를 가리키는 심볼릭 링크일 때, kubelet이 이를 거부하지 않고 자동으로 인증을 시도해 kubelet 계정의 NetNTLMv2 해시가 노출될 수 있습니다. 원문은 이 해시를 크랙하거나, 노드가 도메인에 가입되어 있다면 릴레이해 노드를 사칭할 수 있다고 설명하며, CVSS 5.8(MEDIUM), 원격 악용 가능 여부 True, 공개일 2026-10-26으로 표기되어 있습니다.

items.title: Microsoft offers mass buyouts for roughly a quarter of its workforce
items.content:
Microsoft is offering buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the company tries to control its head count while avoiding layoffs.

The Redmond-based tech giant announced Monday morning that eligible employees at the vice president level and below in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom would receive a “voluntary exit offer” of a standard severance package, based on their location. They’ll have until early December to decide.

In a memo to employees, Microsoft Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said the move was building off the voluntary retirement program earlier this year , which was available to more than 8,700 U.S.-based employees, roughly one-third of whom took the offer.

“This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support,” Coleman wrote. “It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs.”

Multiple organizations within Microsoft are fully participating in the company’s buyout program including the gaming, Windows, Copilot, human resources and finance divisions, according to a screenshot of an internal memo viewed by The Seattle Times. Microsoft’s artificial intelligence, legal and cloud teams are partially participating. Organizations such as marketing, commercial business and security will not be participating.

Since May 2025, Microsoft has been trying to reduce its corporate workforce, first through waves of mass layoffs and now through more creative buyout programs. The company laid off about 15,000 employees last year over the course of several months, affecting about 3,200 Washington-based workers.

Microsoft said it was enacting layoffs to create a flatter, more nimble company, with fewer layers of management and more accountability per employee, essentially blurring the line between employee and manager. The company was also cutting costs as its capital expenditures – investments in AI-related infrastructure – ballooned in 2024 and kept growing in 2025. Microsoft said earlier this year it plans to spend $190 billion on custom computer chips and data centers in 2025, fueled by AI demand.

Layoffs have continued this year, however they’ve been smaller and have mostly affected the company’s gaming division , which is under new leadership and in the middle of a hard reset.

But after last year’s layoffs, leadership took note of the souring culture. Microsoft was posting better financial results and bringing in more cash than ever, while employees felt blindsided by layoffs . After Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella addressed this incongruence in July 2025, Coleman and others spent the past year trying to reshape the company amid an AI-driven shift.

Coleman said in July that Microsoft’s workforce reductions were not driven by AI, at least not by what people would expect. Microsoft says it is not replacing workers by AI agents or workflows. But aside from cost-cutting measures, the company says its various workforce reduction efforts are geared toward shedding outdated roles and teams  as AI changes the business.

In response to the AI-driven platform shift, Microsoft is trying to reskill and relocate workers and is still hiring, keeping its overall head count relatively flat over the past few years. Even after massive layoffs last year, the company’s workforce only dipped by 5,000 between 2025 and 2026 .

Earlier this year, Microsoft President Brad Smith told The Seattle Times that the company’s Redmond workforce of about 52,000 remained relatively unchanged over the past year, despite thousands of workers affected by layoffs. The company credited that to reskilling efforts and increased hiring for new teams.

items.title: Why is it so expensive to send an email?
items.summary: email
items.content:
Why is it so expensive to send an email?

Sending an email is essentially the same as making an HTTPS request. You open a TCP connection to port 25, you do a little SSL handshake, and you send some data through. Most personal computers out there can easily do this thousands of times per second, so how can companies charge $15 to send 1000 emails?! Why do I need some 3rd party company involved at all?! I used to work at Google specifically on GMail, and nothing from my little corner of the product on the “tabbed inbox” team led me to a clear answer...

Unfortunately for me, I was determined to figure it out for myself!

I mostly program with Haskell, and I call C code as necessary for things like OpenSSL and SQLite. I already had a setup for making HTTPS requests from my Haskell code with OpenSSL. I had code for working with HTTP 1.1 messages. How hard could it be to adapt this to email? To my surprise, it turns out that the actual “sending” part is not that hard. The real problem was ultimately out of my hands...

Just like the original plaintext Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP 1.1), there is a correspondingly goofy plaintext protocol for sending emails called Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). The original version of the protocol involves sending a bunch of messages back and forth and back and forth between the sender and receiver. It looks kind of like a little conversation. Here is an example where I start my messages with keywords like HELO and MAIL FROM and the receiver starts her messages with status codes like 220 and 250 :

250 Hello evancz.dev, I am glad to meet you

From: "Evan from Elm" <devnull@evancz.dev>

To: "Alice from Cryptography" <alice@example.com>

I loved your collaboration with Rivest, Shamir, and Adleman

in 1977. I have been eagerly awaiting the invention of email,

so that I could express my admiration through this plaintext

So to send a single email, you originally had to do SEVEN roundtrips! And TLS did not exist at that time, so you did not even get any encryption after all those roundtrips!

That said, it is not that hard to send and receive a bunch of goofy plaintext, so I set it up and sent an email to myself. It worked! But... it showed up in spam.

The original protocol has a very serious flaw. How does mail.example.com know that I am devnull@evancz.dev and not an imposter? The original protocol lets you just claim whatever sender you want, so anybody in the whole world could easily spoof the domain and sender.

So these days you need to add some TXT records to the DNS for your domain. This way the receiver can go look up some public encryption keys for evancz.dev and confirm that whoever sent the email at least has access to the private key.

At this point I started wondering, wait, how do you prevent someone from spoofing the DNS records? Like what if the NSA and AT&T were collaborating or what if the CIA had a history of creating companies like Crypto AG to backdoor cryptographic systems from the very beginning ? It seems like a problem... But hey, I just want to send an email and it looks like all you have to do is set up these DNS records.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees. Read the memo.
items.content:
Microsoft is offering buyouts, according to a memo Chief People Officer Amy Coleman sent to employees Monday.

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Coleman wrote.

Microsoft's voluntary exit offer is the company's latest attempt to slim its workforce without another round of involuntary cuts. After spending heavily on AI infrastructure and reducing headcount this year, Microsoft is offering remaining employees a chance to leave, testing whether voluntary departures can cut costs.

Eligible employees in the US, Canada, India, and the UK at level 70, which includes senior leaders at the company and below, will receive an email later Monday with the terms of the offer. Only some teams are participating, excluding sales organizations, certain engineering teams, and some corporate functions.

Around 60,000 employees — or more than a quarter of the company's workforce — about will be eligible, a spokesperson told Business Insider, and the terms will be similar to Microsoft's standard severance.

The US severance package offered when Microsoft laid off employees earlier this year included a minimum of 60 days of base pay, during which employees will remain on the payroll, and, for most employees, up to 39 weeks of base pay, based on seniority and tenure.

Employees at internal levels 64 and below received one week of base pay per six months of service, for example, and employees at levels 65 to 67 will receive two weeks of base pay per six months of service, according to offers reviewed by Business Insider.

Eligible employees will have until early December to decide whether to take the offer and exit at the end of the year, and there are no plans for another buyout at this time, Microsoft's spokesperson said.

The buyout offer follows Microsoft's Voluntary Retirement Program, which offered a retirement buyout to about 9,000 eligible employees based on age and tenure.

Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.

About one-third of eligible employees took the buyout , in line with expectations, a person familiar with the turnout told Business Insider in June. That buyout allowed Microsoft to lay off a smaller percentage of its workforce than last year, the person said at the time.

Today, we're introducing a new Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to eligible employees within participating organizations. This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating orgs another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs.

The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.

This offer will be available to eligible employees in participating teams in Canada, India, United Kingdom and United States at level 70 and below. This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources. Some organizations are providing the Voluntary Exit Offer, and some are not. Participation varies based on each business's priorities, customer commitments, and workforce needs.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

마치 테러리스트가 인질극 벌이는데 인질 죽는다고 테러리스트 진압 안하겠다는 것과 같은 말이다.

총수, 의장 검찰 총원해서 조져 놓다가 사면을 해놓으니까 버릇이 안좋아 진건지 아니면 반도체좀 했다고 뭐가 된양인지 모르겠다만

items.title: Sebastian Raschka's from-scratch video course on building reasoning models
items.content:
Building Reasoning Models from the Ground Up: A Full Video Course

Eight videos and over 11 hours of coding, covering evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation in Python and PyTorch.

I have written a lot about reasoning models here over the last two years on Ahead of AI, including a recent article on mechanisms to control reasoning effort levels in contemporary LLMs . Reasoning models are still as relevant as ever. In fact, almost all current-generation LLMs today are reasoning models or offer a reasoning mode.

For those who are interested in how reasoning models work, including inference scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation, I wrote my recent Build Reasoning Model (From Scratch), which implements these from the ground up in PyTorch, which, in my experience, is still the best way to understand and learn how things really work.

Now, in the last few months, I also sat down and recorded accompanying lectures I wanted to share with you. So, below, you will find eight reasoning model-from-scratch coding videos (11 hours of content).

We start with a pre-trained LLM and implement methods to evaluate and improve it in Python and PyTorch. So, if you enjoyed my Coding LLMs from the Ground Up course last year, this is essentially the sequel (but you can also watch it without the prior course as a prerequisite).

I’m currently taking a short break and will be back soon with more exciting LLM research roundups next month. In the meantime, I hope you enjoy coding along!

How LLMs, reasoning models, and agents relate and fit together

As a small side note, and since I often get asked how reasoning models relate to today’s AI agents, here’s a short section on this before getting started with the videos.

A reasoning model is essentially an upgrade from a conventional LLM, that is, adding more post-training via reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (and optionally inference scaling techniques) to make it more capable of solving more challenging problems. Classically, reasoning models are developed for math and code, but the capabilities can generalize to other problem domains as well.

A reasoning model then functions as the engine inside an agent harness, where the agent harness is a software or tooling framework around the LLM/reasoning model to tackle even more challenging problems (bigger coding tasks, travel booking, and all other sorts of personal assistant tasks). The task of the harness is sophisticated context management and giving the LLM access to tools.

Figure 1: An engine analogy for conventional LLMs, reasoning models, and agent harnesses. Figure from my Components of a Coding Agent article.

In this analogy depicted in the figure above, the model is the engine, and the agent harness adds the machinery that lets us use it for various things (as an upgrade from a simple chatbot interface). An agent can use either a conventional LLM or a reasoning model, but reasoning models are the more typical choice as they are more capable. (As mentioned above, most current-gen LLMs are reasoning models with variable reasoning effort settings.)

So, the bottom line is that reasoning models, as the “engine,” remain an important part of understanding modern LLM agents.

The resources accompanying these topics shown above are:

The Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) book and videos

The Build A Reasoning Model (From Scratch) book (and videos below)

The Components of a Coding Agent article on Substack

The videos below focus on developing the reasoning model that can power such a system.

The reasoning-from-scratch videos focus on a small pre-trained Qwen3 model, where we implement the reasoning methods ourselves in Python and PyTorch. Starting with a pre-trained model lets us focus on the interesting part: evaluation, inference-time scaling, reinforcement learning, and distillation.

items.content_ko: 제작자는 Gram이 rustls-webpki와 webpki-roots 패키지를 포함해 배포되어 취약하다는 내용을 전달받았다고 밝히며, 모든 사용자에게 3.4.0으로 가능한 한 빨리 업그레이드할 것을 권장합니다. 이번 릴리스는 이 문제 때문만은 아니고 새 버전을 태그할 때가 되었기 때문이라고 설명합니다. 많은 수정과 훌륭한 새 기능이 들어갔으며, 편집기 개선에 기여한 분들에게 감사를 전합니다. 주요 변경점으로는 @iskrant_x가 기여한 Git diff 나란히 보기, @kbilkis의 탭 바 줄바꿈 옵션, @yilmazer가 백포트한 Helix 'Amp Jump'(gw) 기능, @nicoco가 작업한 Git 패널의 커밋 기록 보기가 있습니다. 또한 서버 바이너리를 찾지 못하면 설치 명령을 제안하는 기능(#485, @xmort)도 추가되었습니다. 전체 목록은 아직 불완전하며, 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있습니다.

items.title: Microsoft offers buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs
items.content:
Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, according to its annual filing. David Paul Morris / Bloomberg via Getty

Oct. 26, 2026, 2:06 PM EDT / Source : Reuters

Microsoft said Monday it is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, or more than a quarter of its global workforce, as the technology giant looks to contain costs and help fund its massive AI investments.

Staffers across the Windows maker would be eligible for the offers, including those working in AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, a source familiar with the matter told Reuters, requesting anonymity as the matter was private. Units such as marketing, commercial business and security will be excluded, the source added.

“This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs,” Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said in a staff memo.

Like other tech giants, Microsoft is spending hundreds of billions of dollars on AI data centers and chips, drawing scrutiny from investors over whether the returns will justify the staggering cost. The company, slated to report first-quarter results after markets close Wednesday, has forecast $175 billion in capital expenditures for the 2026 calendar year.

Microsoft had 223,000 full-time employees globally as of June 30, according to its annual filing.

Shares of Microsoft, which had risen about 10% this year, were up about 1% on Monday. The development was first reported by Business Insider.

items.title_ko: Microsoft, 비용 통제 위해 약 6만 명에게 자발적 퇴직 제안
items.summary_ko: Microsoft는 비용을 관리하고 AI 투자 재원을 마련하기 위해 전 세계 직원의 4분의 1이 넘는 약 6만 명에게 자발적 퇴직 제안을 한다고 밝혔습니다. 연례 보고서 기준 6월 30일 현재 정규직 직원은 전 세계 22만 3,000명이었습니다. 대상에는 AI 경험, Copilot, 재무, 인사, Xbox, Windows+Devices 조직이 포함되며, 마케팅, 상업 사업, 보안 부서는 제외됩니다.
items.content_ko: Microsoft는 월요일 비용을 관리하고 대규모 AI 투자를 지원하기 위해 약 6만 명에게 자발적 퇴직 제안을 한다고 밝혔습니다. 이는 전 세계 직원의 4분의 1이 넘는 규모입니다. 소식통에 따르면 AI 경험, Copilot, 재무, 인사, Xbox, Windows+Devices 등 여러 조직이 대상이며, 마케팅, 상업 사업, 보안 부서는 제외됩니다. 콜먼 최고인사책임자는 직원 메모에서 이번 제안이 회사 밖의 미래를 고민하는 직원에게 지원과 함께 전환할 새로운 선택지를 준다고 밝혔습니다. 또 참여 조직이 변화하는 필요에 맞춰 인력을 조정할 또 다른 방법을 얻는다고 설명했습니다. 기사는 다른 빅테크처럼 Microsoft도 AI 데이터센터와 칩에 수천억 달러를 쓰고 있다고 전합니다. 이러한 대규모 투자가 외부의 면밀한 주목을 받고 있다는 내용이 이어지지만 본문이 중간에서 끊겨 있습니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Birdwatching rewires the brain and slows cognitive decline
items.content:
Birdwatching rewires the brain and slows cognitive decline

4 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google

Birdwatching can help slow brain ageing and is increasingly being used as therapy for dementia patients.

Every week, a group of elderly birders spend hours hunkering down inside a wooden hide in the English countryside, peering through binoculars as they excitedly share what they spot. An oystercatcher's long, bright beak probing the pebbled ground; two great crested grebes bobbing in the water, their plumed heads poised.

Most of these birdwatchers have difficulty recalling what happened earlier that day, and might struggle to follow a conversation. But they become animated when swapping notes on the birds that fill the sky around Forge Mill Lake in the UK's West Midlands.

Among them is 78-year-old Harold*. He loved the outdoors when he was younger, but more recently dementia has made him withdrawn and anxious. His daughter Lucy* brought him here, hoping that the change of scenery and peaceful lake might be good for him. After an apprehensive start, Harold began smiling when someone pointed out a robin and enjoyed watching the ducks splashing in the water. Blue tits darted between the nearby trees, and Lucy saw Harold laugh for the first time in a long time.

"For that moment in time he was present in the moment, he wasn't worried about his memory or his confidence. That is very powerful, in a gentle way," says Jenny Budinger, a community dementia advisor at Age UK, the non-profit that runs the birdwatching group.

Birdwatching is increasingly recognised as a valuable way for elderly people and dementia patients to spend their time, with groups set up in nursing homes in the UK, Germany and the US. Paying attention to birds , even through the window, can help older people feel more connected to others, experience more positive emotions and boost memory skills. Now new research shows that birdwatching can reshape the brain, much like learning an athletic sport or a musical instrument – and may even help slow the brain's ageing.

In the laboratory, neuroscientists tested keen birdwatchers' identification skills to determine who was an expert and who was a novice, then looked at their brains. The scientists found that the very structure of experts' brains was different – and that birdwatching expertise might slow age-related decline by keeping the brain more organised.

Erik Wing, who led this research at Baycrest Academy for Research and Education in Toronto, Canada, compared MRI brain scans from bird experts to those of novices while they identified birds. He found that expert brains were wired differently in regions important for functions like attention, visual perception and visual recognition.

Among expert birders, these regions showed more activity – particularly when they were asked to identify birds they weren't already familiar with. The findings don't prove whether structural brain differences are the cause or effect of birdwatching expertise. But, Wing says, one explanation is that the areas of the brain used for birdwatching might undergo "neuroplasticity" – the ability to change shape and function over time.

Birdwatching can reshape the brain and may help slow ageing (Credit: BBC/Serenity Strull)

Wing also analysed how organised the birdwatchers' brains were. Organisation in the brain tends to reduce with age, and lower measures of organisation are associated with reduced cognition . In experts' brains, some regions had higher levels of organisation and coherence than novices of the same age. Some of these regions were also the ones that showed more activity during bird identification. This indicates a "kind of preservation of organisation" in the brains of experts as they age, Wing says.

items.title: About the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs
items.summary: mac, security
items.content:
Apple is blocking the compromised certificates automatically. Mac administrators can take optional steps for some command-line tools.

Since 19 October 2026, Apple has been blocking the certificates of the compromised eMudhra intermediate Certification Authorities (CAs) that issue TLS certificates, and is making additional updates to this block.

If you don't use Terminal as part of your workflow, you don't need to do anything. Your Apple devices now automatically block these certificates in Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple's networking and security frameworks.

If you use Terminal as part of your workflow (such as system administrators or developers), you might use command-line tools that can still accept these certificates. Some tools included with macOS or the Xcode Command Line Tools — like curl and git — check certificates against /etc/ssl/cert.pem and can still accept these certificates until a future software update. To stop those tools from accepting them sooner, you can remove root CA certificates from the file.

The private keys of eight intermediate CAs operated by eMudhra were compromised. Two of these CAs issue code signing certificates, which Apple's frameworks don't trust. The other six issue TLS certificates. Someone with keys from these six CAs could create certificates that appear valid for any website. eMudhra and Sectigo have revoked the affected certificates.

Each of the 6 TLS intermediate CAs has two certificates, for 12 in total:

A certificate issued by emSign Root TLS CA - G3, which chains to emSign ECC Root CA - G3

A certificate cross-signed by Sectigo, which chains to AAA Certificate Services

On 19 October 2026, Apple began blocking these 12 certificates on Apple devices. Updates to certificate configuration data are sent to devices automatically and as needed, so you don't need to install a software update to get this change. Apple is making additional updates to this block, which will also be delivered automatically. On 23 October 2026, Apple also began blocking the emSign ECC Root CA - G3.

Apple is making further changes to block these certificates in other places on Mac where software checks certificates, such as the command-line tools included with macOS or the Xcode Command Line Tools that use /etc/ssl/cert.pem. These changes will be available in a future software update, and you won't need to edit any files to get them.

Most users don't need to edit /etc/ssl/cert.pem. Safari, Mail, and apps that use Apple's networking and security frameworks don't use this file, and your Apple devices block these certificates in them automatically.

On Mac, some command-line tools included with macOS or the Xcode Command Line Tools (including curl, git, python3, ruby, perl, and openssl) check certificates against /etc/ssl/cert.pem. For certificates that chain to a root CA certificate in this file, these tools don't check Apple's block or whether the certificate has been revoked. This file will be updated in a future macOS update. If you use these tools and don't want to wait for the update, you can remove root CA certificates from the file.

Some apps and tools include their own list of root CA certificates and don't use Apple's block or /etc/ssl/cert.pem. For those apps or tools, contact the developer .

Rather than wait for the upcoming software update, administrators can choose to remove the root CA certificates to which the blocked certificates chain from /etc/ssl/cert.pem.

These steps affect every tool that uses /etc/ssl/cert.pem. Afterward, tools that use only this file might not be able to verify some websites whose certificates chain to these root CA certificates through intermediate CAs that weren't affected.

A macOS software update can replace /etc/ssl/cert.pem with Apple's version. Until you install the software update that includes Apple's changes, run the command in step 4 after each software update. If it lists a root CA certificate that you removed, the update replaced the file.…

items.content_ko: Apple은 침해된 eMudhra 중간 CA가 발급한 TLS 인증서를 2026년 10월 19일부터 차단하고 있으며, 이 차단을 추가로 업데이트하고 있습니다. 터미널을 사용하지 않는 사용자는 조치가 필요 없습니다. 터미널을 쓰는 시스템 관리자와 개발자의 경우, macOS나 Xcode Command Line Tools에 포함된 curl, git 같은 도구가 /etc/ssl/cert.pem을 기준으로 검사하기 때문에 향후 소프트웨어 업데이트 전까지 이 인증서를 계속 허용할 수 있습니다. 이를 더 일찍 막으려면 해당 파일에서 루트 CA 인증서를 제거하면 됩니다. eMudhra가 운영하는 중간 CA 8개의 개인 키가 유출되었으며, 이 중 2개는 코드 서명 인증서를 발급합니다.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Some iPhone Duo screens are already failing
items.content:
The iPhone Duo launched last week, offering anyone willing to spend $2,000 a chance to experience Apple’s first foldable phone. For some early buyers, the morning after isn’t going great. Despite the company’s big talk about its “precision-engineered” hinge, some devices appear to have a hardware flaw that destroys the device’s impressive internal display within hours (or minutes) of use.

The Internet is currently overflowing with images of busted iPhone Duos, all sporting almost identical damage. The OLED is marred by several bright lines originating just below the midpoint of the display. These bands of damaged pixels extend all the way to the bottom and right edges. Some units also show lines of dead pixels following the crease from the top to the area where the bright lines begin.

Anyone who has seen a damaged OLED panel will be familiar with this type of defect. When the layers of the display are damaged, the pixels no longer receive the correct voltage to illuminate them. Instead, they get the full driving voltage and are permanently on at maximum brightness. Some pixels can get no voltage, leaving them totally black. The only fix is to replace the OLED, but swapping the iPhone Duo’s screen reportedly costs half as much as the device itself.

It sounds like most affected devices are failing within about a day of use. But a few unlucky buyers note they only opened and closed the phone a few times , and in some cases, they hadn’t even finished the initial setup process. Some customers have reported success taking their defective phones to Apple stores for replacement, but spares may be in short supply right now.

In the absence of any official explanation, iFixit may be the next best thing. The site has already torn an iPhone Duo apart and taken a close look at the affected area. After years of seeing other foldables fail, there are a few suspects to check. Since foldables need to pass data and power across the hinge, there’s always a cable tucked in there that could press on the screen. The iPhone Duo has a wide cable with “accordion-like pleats,” according to iFixit, but this doesn’t quite match the accounts of the damage.

People with broken $2,000 iPhones say there’s unusual physical resistance and sometimes even a clicking sound as the device closes. After that, the lines appear. Using CT scans of the phone, iFixit has shown that the point of failure starts below where the ribbon cable passes through the hinge. The width of the supporting hinge mechanism changes in that spot, suggesting a mechanical misalignment.

A possible explanation for iPhone Duo failures.

A possible explanation for iPhone Duo failures.

The animation above shows iFixit’s best guess at what’s happening. The support bar in that narrowed section of the hinge may be getting stuck, preventing it from dropping far enough to accommodate the waterdrop bend in the OLED panel when the device closes. This creates stress on the display that ultimately damages the matrix. YouTuber CuriousHagi also zeroed in on that region, identifying a place where the thinner link may be snapping during operation. He speculates the component is physically sticking to the support plate.

If this fiddly little hinge piece is the culprit, there’s no way to prevent the OLED on an affected device from failing. It could happen after five minutes or five days, but continuous pressure on an OLED panel will eventually lead to permanent damage.

Apple has yet to acknowledge the issue, and it probably won’t have anything to say until the problem is fully investigated. The scale is impossible to know—Apple sells a lot of devices, so even a low failure rate could see a flood of reports on social media. Adding moving parts to a phone will lead to at least some increase in hardware issues. Apple certainly wouldn’t be the first device maker to have problems with its first foldable launch.

items.summary_ko: 지난주 출시된 2,000달러짜리 iPhone Duo 중 일부는 사용 몇 시간(또는 몇 분) 만에 내장 디스플레이가 손상되는 하드웨어 결함을 보이는 것으로 전해졌습니다. 온라인에 올라온 사진들은 거의 동일한 형태의 손상을 보여주는데, 화면 중앙 아래에서 시작해 하단과 오른쪽 가장자리까지 이어지는 밝은 선들과, 접힘선을 따라 나타난 죽은 픽셀 줄이 특징입니다. 본문은 OLED 층이 손상되면 픽셀이 최대 밝기로 계속 켜지거나 완전히 꺼지며, 이를 고칠 방법은 OLED를 교체하는 것뿐이라고 설명합니다.
items.content_ko: Apple이 정밀 설계를 강조한 힌지에도 불구하고, 일부 iPhone Duo 기기에서 내장 디스플레이가 몇 분에서 몇 시간 안에 손상된다는 보고가 나왔습니다. 손상 사진들은 화면 중앙 바로 아래에서 시작해 하단과 오른쪽 가장자리까지 뻗는 여러 개의 밝은 선을 공통적으로 보여주며, 접힘선을 따라 위에서 밝은 선이 시작되는 지점까지 이어지는 죽은 픽셀 줄도 나타납니다. 본문은 OLED 층이 손상되면 픽셀이 올바른 전압을 받지 못해 항상 최대 밝기로 켜지거나 전압을 받지 못해 검게 남는다고 설명합니다. 이 경우 OLED 교체 외에는 해결 방법이 없습니다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: A faster way to compute signed 64-bit floor division by constants
items.summary: c++, performance
items.content:
Signed integer floor division is where you do a/b and get a result that rounds towards − ∞ ,

whereas standard ( “truncated” ) signed division rounds towards 0 .

As stated in Hacker's Delight: “[I suspect that] floor division more often gives the result you want” .

This article is about floor division where the divisor is known at compile time .

Despite the usefulness of this function, the world of integer floor division is in shambles:

This blog post aims to not only shine light on the fast algorithms, but will also introduce a new fast approach which, with ideal compilation:

The benchmark section has a detailed overview showing per-divisor results over many platforms, for throughput and latency.

It works in all bit-widths, and may find use on some 32-bit or SIMD applications, but the biggest benefit is in 64-bit.

It also can be used for faster positive-modulus, and faster "Euclidean" division (differs to floor division for negative divisors) .

Floor division can be much faster than you probably realise.

Below is a snapshot throughput benchmark for division by 86400 (the number of seconds in one day) , the kind of performance you can expect using most languages' built-in methods, vs fast alternatives outlined in this blog.

Floor Div 86400 throughput - ARM64 Chips As tested on MacBook Pro M4 Pro

Floor Div 86400 throughput - X86 Chips As tested on AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D

*Rust provides "div_euclid", which matches floor-div for positive divisors.

See the benchmark section for a deeper comparison across over 40 divisors.

Since some people visiting this page will be just looking to copy/paste code, I'll start with this function builder on the right:

For the avoidance of doubt, the license only applies if you copy/paste the comment and code verbatim. No license is required if you re-write the same logic in your code.

A set of 65535 divisors from -32768 to 32767 for 64-bit can be generated into a single self-contained C++ file. It includes a boundary test in the same file.

See the comment at the top of the download for how to build and run it.

Using this form, you can choose any bit-width and any divisor to get a copy/paste function ready to go.

There is also reference algorithm (a reusable C++ template with additional microarchitectural performance tweaks) .

As you can see, the technique is so simple that I'd expect that somebody has done this before, but I've looked around and not found it documented anywhere. If it turns out to have been done before, at least this page will make it discoverable.

For the rest of us, I'll cover a narrative about floor division, which matches my process of discovery... And if you want to create a fast library or compiler/language implementation, this will be your one-stop shop.

If you want to skip the history lesson, you can jump straight to the new stuff .

Let's suppose you want to convert a Unix timestamp measured in seconds, to rata-die (a day count). And let's also suppose you forgot how to do this properly, and you use standard ("truncated") division.

We need to divide by 86400 (60×60×24) . We'll use a 64-bit timestamp, since a 32-bit timestamp can only hold about ±68 years.

You'll be very happy with this implementation on the right until somebody hands you a timestamp before 1970!

The above function returns incorrect results for most negative values.

Of course, you should be using floor division , the type of division that's useful for tracking repeating patterns like timestamps, angle rotations, tile positions etc. This is the type of division where the associated "%" operation is a proper positive modulus , not that fake modulus that " % " provides in C++, JavaScript etc.

items.summary_ko: 부호 있는 정수의 floor 나눗셈은 결과를 음의 무한대 방향으로 내림하며, 0 방향으로 버리는 일반 나눗셈과 다릅니다. 이 글은 제수가 컴파일 시점에 알려진 경우를 다루며, 모든 비트 폭에서 동작하고 특히 64비트에서 이점이 큰 새로운 고속 기법을 소개합니다. 하루의 초 수인 86400으로 나누는 경우를 예로 든 벤치마크도 함께 제시합니다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Americans Are Officially More Scared of AI Than a Loved One Getting Cancer: "We expect concerns about AI to remain a significant part of the national conversation in the years ahead."
items.content:
The fear of AI has reached a fever pitch.

There’s data to support it. According to the Chapman University Survey of American Fears , an annual poll that asks what Americans are “really afraid of,” the fear of AI hurting the political process and economy ranked in third and seventh place, respectively.

These fears were only outdone by “corrupt government officials” and the possibility of the US becoming involved in another world war. Perhaps the most extraordinary context: anxieties about AI are scaring Americans more than the fear of a loved one “becoming seriously ill,” or “people I love dying.”

Put simply, according to the survey, people are more scared of AI than a loved one getting a terminal diagnosis — a grim indication of just how much head space fears of AI are taking up for the average person.

Other surveys have turned up similar findings. Just last month, a Politico poll found that roughly two thirds of Americans believes there’s now at least a “moderate” chance that advanced AI could destroy humanity.

“These findings make it clear that Americans are concerned not just about what AI might mean for their jobs, but about its potential impact on our political system and the economy,” said Chapman University professor of sociology and survey founder Christopher Bader in a statement . “As artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into everyday life, understanding these fears will be increasingly important.”

“We expect concerns about AI to remain a significant part of the national conversation in the years ahead,” he added.

At the same time, the exact ranking should be taken with a grain of salt.

“I think it’s important to keep in mind that the top 10 doesn’t tell the full story, and even though a lot of fears went up this year, there are a lot of fears that are also actually lower,” said Chapman University sociology associate professor Ashley Wendell Kranjac in the statement. For instance, fewer Americans listed air pollution or terrorist attacks compared to last year.

However, we’ve already seen that many of these fears are well-founded. The tech industry is essentially betting the fate of the entire economy by making colossal investments in data centers, massive investments that may not only fail to pay off , but could even cause global markets to collapse if the bubble bursts. Political candidates are also spending obscene amounts on AI slop in an effort to influence the upcoming midterm elections.

In short, it’s no wonder Americans are terrified of what AI hath wrought.

More on AI fears: The Majority of Americans Are Now Terrified of AI

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: CSS-Tricks has a new owner
items.summary: web
items.content:
NVIDIA L4 GPUs. 5-second cold starts. Scale to zero when idle.

This is pretty wild, but let’s get right to it because it’s big news:

CSS-Tricks is an independent site once again!

Just to recap:  DigitalOcean purchased CSS-Tricks in 2022  from Chris Coyier, who founded the site in 2007. Chris ran it all the way up to that purchase.

Here we are in 2026, and I’m taking independent ownership of the site.

So, wait, who owns the site? That’d be me. (Wow, never imagined I would get to say that!) Of course, I have  a small, awesome team  to help with the day-to-day management of the site.

That all said, I do envision that some things will change. In fact, I’m planning that they will change in what I hope are very good ways. Maybe a question-answer thing makes sense here since this is very much an evolving discussion.

Yes, I’ve got the keys to the castle, so to speak. And, even after 12 years of working on the site, I’ll admit I’m a little overwhelmed and nervous about that. I mean, it’s an investment for sure, as you can imagine, and I’m making this my full-time job. At least for a while.

I want to make CSS-Tricks both a real community and a place that’s inclusive of  everyone , no matter where they are in their front-end learning journey. That’s going to take some work and time.

My latest IPO launched, and I’m now worth one trillion dollars. Wait, wait. That’s not right.

It’s going to be hard. Advertising will certainly be needed now. But, in order to keep the lights on, I’ll have to approach them differently.

In the pre-DigitalOcean days we sold real ad packages with things like display ads, sponsored posts, newsletter sponsors, and the like. As an independent website, we will need to return to our advertising roots.

So, if you’re in a place looking to advertise,  please do reach out !

Right?! Ad revenue can’t be the only thing paying the bills. I have lots of ideas and several plates already spinning. Like, I’ve been neck deep in developing an HTML/CSS course for beginners.

(And you can now support the site by becoming a member  — thanks in advance!)

Educational content has been in the dumps lately, right? Again, I’m hoping that CSS-Tricks will be more inclusive, no matter where you or anyone else is at in the learning journey. This place has traditionally been for folks who know what they’re doing. But I’m truly committed to creating more entry points for those getting started, particularly as  our field is in the early throes of a growing skills gap .

And yes, I do believe that  learning the basics is more important now than ever . But what learning actually looks like is what’s key. Front-end courses are  down across the board . It has to be done differently.

There are other things in the works, but I think a course is one of the first things you’ll see.

Oh, and  the newsletter . That’s coming back after a way-too-long hiatus.

That’s still very much a thing! We’ll keep our regularly scheduled broadcast going.

But maybe a little less than you’re used to. Those articles are part of the investment I’m making. Expect maybe one or two articles most weeks, at least as the ball starts rolling.

That also means the  guest writing form  is back in business! We have a nice backlog of articles through the rest of the year, which is great, but also means new submissions will have to wait a bit.

I won’t be able to accept everything that comes in, but I will absolutely read them and follow-up as best I can.  Unless it’s a slop submission , of course.

Will you be writing most of the articles to save cost?

Nah! My goal is to make CSS-Tricks a platform that gives folks a voice to share great ideas. I think we all prefer that over me just using it as my own soapbox. I’ve written plenty for this site the past 12 years. I’m happier (and more comfortable) being behind the curtain and giving others the full spotlight.

I may be writing a bit, developing the site here and there, editing a small stack of article drafts, or…

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: US scientists detect incoming drones from 49 feet using motor signals
items.content:
A new passive sensing approach has been designed to detect and identify micro-unmanned aerial systems (micro-UAS/drones) near critical infrastructure.

Every electric drone in the sky carries some sort of signature. It isn’t an encrypted radio ping or a flashing LED light, but an invisible, unavoidable hum: the extremely low-frequency (ELF) magnetic field thrown off by its spinning brushless motors.

Now, researchers at Florida International University (FIU) have figured out how to use ELF to spot incoming threat drones without firing a single signal into the air.

Drones have advanced modern warfare, evolving from high-altitude novelties into cheap, mass-producible airborne weapons. To fight back, the U.S. Department of War requested a $74 billion for drone and counter-drone technologies in its fiscal 2027 budget request. Active radar remains the primary defense against airborne threats, but carries a major vulnerability.

Typical active radar , optical, and acoustic systems face constraints from line-of-sight barriers, environmental background noise, and strict transmission regulations. Passive ELF magnetic sensing reduces these vulnerabilities by covertly capturing motor emissions. This technique operates silently, without broadcasting signals. It offers a stealthy detection alternative unaffected by weather conditions or acoustic interference.

“Every detection method currently in use gives something away. Radar transmits a signal. Acoustic systems get overwhelmed by background noise. We went a different direction entirely,” said Arjuna Madanayake, an Associate Professor at FIU’s College of Engineering & Computing who led the research.

“While the range of our method is limited for now, it costs only a few hundred dollars to develop and could run continuously without any specialized support, unlike radar systems,” Madanayake said.

The FIU team converts a basic physical requirement of drone flight into an effective security trap. Different motor configurations across drone models create unique electromagnetic fingerprints, which could help track and identify specific devices.

The researchers built a specialized circular loop antenna paired with a low-noise analog front end to capture these subtle magnetic waves. And ran the raw signals through a Fast Fourier Transform process to map out spectral correlation patterns, essentially converting raw magnetic hums into distinct visual “maps.”

According to the study, a VGG16-based convolutional neural network (CNN) then takes over, reading the maps to decide whether a drone is nearby and what kind it is.

In outdoor field tests, the system performed with startling precision. It achieved 98.5 percent outdoor detection accuracy at ranges up to 49 feet (15 meters). And 83.5 percent overall accuracy when classifying four distinct scenarios (three separate drone models plus a no-drone baseline).

Although a 49 feet detection range remains modest, the system excels in its stealth and low manufacturing cost. A purely passive receiver emits no signals, making it invisible to hostile forces trying to jam or locate defensive sensors. Electromagnetic fields pass through fog, total darkness, and heavy environmental noise, providing reliable detection where optical and acoustic sensors routinely fail.

“Knowing the type of drone that’s coming matters,” Madanayake said. “Different drones can carry different payloads and have different threat profiles. The more you can tell a defender about what’s coming, the better they can respond.”

The FIU research group is currently partnering with U.S. industry players to boost the system’s detection range. If scaled successfully, low-cost passive magnetic arrays could soon sit silently around power plants, military bases, and critical infrastructure, listening for the invisible signatures of approaching danger.

items.title: 의뢰 맡깁니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Oldest GUI application that still runs on Windows 11
items.summary: historical, windows
items.content:
For a while I’ve been wondering about a silly question, which is, what’s the oldest application with a GUI that will still run on Windows 11 without modifications or emulation.

Given Windows’ excellent backwards compatibility, I expected the answer to be something impressively old.

Sadly, Windows 11 can’t run 16-bit Windows programs by itself, because 64-bit Windows has no NTVDM , so we’re going to have to find something from the early NT era.

I remember asking this question a while ago on an anonymous forum, where someone pointed me to Win32s , and suggested to find an early release version of it with FREECELL.exe .

So I did exactly that, and lo and behold, FREECELL.EXE with a date modified of 22-Feb-93 running and fully playable, without any changes on the latest version of Windows 11:

At the time of this post, that’s a 33 years and 8 months old application, which is impressively almost as old as me.

So I kinda thought “cool”, considered this a solved mystery and forgot about it shortly afterwards. But for some reason, this question popped into my mind again lately and this time I decided to dig deeper to see if I can find something older.

Digging through old Windows versions on the Internet Archive, I found some early NT 3.1 pre-release versions that seemed promising, but the main issue seemed to be either incompatibility with today’s executable format or API changes that came later in development.

The earliest 1991 versions used a draft PE format not compatible with modern Windows, and builds up to mid-1992 assumed the cdecl calling convention instead of stdcall for Windows API calls, so arguments would get removed twice, as such:

call [ShowWindow] ; Win11 ShowWindow is stdcall, ends with "ret 4" and removes them

add esp, 4 ; the 1992 caller removes them again

Which would understandably cause the program to crash.

There was one application that caught my eye though, from Build 347, and that was CDPLAYER.EXE , linked on 16-Nov-1992 . By then the calling convention was fixed, but the other programs in that build crash in their bundled C runtime. CDPLAYER.EXE avoids that by using the system’s crtdll.dll , and Windows 11 still ships a crtdll.dll in SysWOW64 .

If you start the program, you get something like this:

That is because, duh, my computer doesn’t have a CD-ROM drive. But you can use a small DLL ( cdemu.dll ) to emulate one with some fake audio data and actually get it to play audio:

Pretty cool for a program that’s almost 34 years old!

So earlier I mentioned that 16-bit programs are out of the picture because they are no longer supported.

But if you want, you can use something like otvdm to run older Windows applications.

Behold, a fully playable version of REVERSI.EXE dated 15-Nov-1985 running on Windows 11, taken from Windows 1.01:

And although using otvdm does feel like cheating, I thought it was cool enough to include in this post.

items.title: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees
items.content:
Microsoft said Monday that it's offering buyouts to a wide swath of employees as it strives to balance a costly artificial intelligence infrastructure build-out with capital efficiency.

The software maker announced a new voluntary exit offer for certain workers in the U.S., Canada, India and the United Kingdom at its experience level of 70 or below.

Around 60,000 people are eligible, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be named while discussing an internal matter. The effort affects about 27% of Microsoft's total workforce of 223,000 people.

Microsoft has been ramping up spending on data centers to accommodate high AI computing demand, supplying cloud services to Anthropic, OpenAI and a slew of other companies. Capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, Microsoft said in July. In the same quarter a year ago, capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion.

That's put a strain on Microsoft's finances. In April, it announced a first-ever voluntary retirement program that around 7% of U.S. employees were eligible for. Then, in July, Microsoft announced plans to lay off 4,800 employees .

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, wrote in a memo to employees . "This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program."

Microsoft is in the midst of a business model transformation , increasingly trying to charge clients based on how much AI they actually use. It has armed programmers , sellers and supply chain workers with AI tools and observed noticeable results . At the same time, the 51-year-old maker of Windows and Office wants to ensure that it has the right talent to go after its most compelling new growth opportunities.

The idea is to make the shift without weakening Microsoft's financial profile. In the second quarter, cloud rivals Alphabet and Amazon both reported negative free cash flow, but Microsoft showed $19.64 billion in positive free cash flow for the period, down 23% year over year.

Some marketing, sales and engineering teams have decided not to participate in the new buyout, the person said. Employees must decide whether to take the offer in early December, and those participating will leave on Dec. 31, the person added.

More than 30% of those who could join the voluntary retirement program went ahead with it, Microsoft said in July . But that was open to those at the senior director level and below, while the new initiative goes higher, to the vice president level, said the person briefed on the new plan. The person said Microsoft does not have a target in mind this time around.

On Wednesday, Microsoft is scheduled to report third-quarter results.

items.title: Blaise Pascal invented fixed route public transport (2024)
items.content:
Blaise Pascal knew he was dying.  He was in his 30s and had been sick most of his life, but at least he didn’t have to worry about being forgotten.  He had already made transformative innovations in mathematics, physics, philosophy, and theology, and in his spare time he was assembling a collection of thoughts about God that would become the Pensées , which has been praised as some of the finest prose ever written in the French language.  He was fortunate to live at a time (the mid-1600s) when, if you were born to the right parents, nobody told you you needed to specialize.

So what did he do with the last lucid days of his life?  He invented fixed route public transport.

The vehicle used by Pascal’s service. Note that each had a fixed sign advertising the endpoints of the route. But who cares about the vehicle? What matters is the service.  Source: Taras Grescoe’s Substack .

Wikipedia currently says he invented the bus line, but that’s too narrow. Pascal’s network, which he called carrosses a cinq sols or “five penny carriages” used eight-passenger horse-drawn carriages, but they did what fixed route public transport does.  They operated predictable frequencies along multiple connecting routes, forming a network.  This is not just the ancestor of every city bus, but also of every train or tram.

Had this really not been done before?  Apparently not on land. Ferries are an ancient idea, both for crossing water bodies and for traveling along them.  They are fixed routes, of course, but that’s mostly because the shore is fixed.  Pascal’s idea was that even though carriages could go from anywhere to anywhere on Paris’s street network, a special kind of usefulness would arise if they didn’t do that, but instead followed paths that people could remember and plan around.

Here is the map of his complete network design:

Frequency ranged from 7.5 minutes to 15 minutes, so these came often enough that people could just go out and wait for them, not worrying about a schedule.  Their main failure was overcrowding and pass-ups, which of course is a kind of success.  Obviously, someone needed to invent a larger horse-drawn vehicle for this purpose, but that would wait a while still.  The first line began on March 18, 1662 and the whole network was operating by July, just before Pascal’s death, a pace of implementation that is hard to imagine today.  It’s likely that Pascal spent many of his final days thinking about this, when he wasn’t writing immortal prose about God.

Gazing at the map, I recognize many of the eternal principles of fixed route transit planning:  The lines try to remain far from each other, converging only on major destinations.  They are often perpendicular, which maximizes the odds that a connection between those routes will make lots of trips possible.  There are more or less straight lines running across the city — because where demand is spread uniformly, a straight line is more likely to match people’s desires than a winding one — and there’s an orbital line, yellow on the map, that goes all the way around the edge in a two way loop.  Orbitals are a common shape because they make such effective connections with radial lines, and their length means they connect an unusual number of origins and destinations directly.

At age 11, Pascal had re-derived much of Euclid’s geometry from scratch because his father kept the books from him, thinking he was still too young.  So, dying at 38, Pascal probably could sense that these principles were mathematically right, even though they’d never been written down before.

But as a network designer I wanted to know more.  How did this map come about?  Did Pascal ever explain the design himself? What explains the biggest exceptions to the principles?  The routes aren’t as straight as they could be.  And why do so many of the lines converge at Luxembourg Palace in the southwest?  Much of the government was around there, but still, was that really such a hub of citywide demand?  I…
